It wasn't until I was older that I fully began to appreciate how red-pilled the film children of men really was. When I first saw it as a kid I didn't think much of it. I knew it had excellent world building and described an apocalyptic scenario rarely considered. But I just assumed the attitude toward immigration reflect european values of the time.

However looking back on it through a modern lens I can't help but see it as a stark warning. Of things to come as well as what is happening now. In terms of setting you had massive third world immigration. Years of declining global production and standard of living meant that people would risk life and limb to pour into wealthy countries. In order to survive and still provide basic services england tried to put up a wall but it was too little too late. It was left with massive melanin enriched ghettos that were dens of violent criminality, drug smuggling, and corruption. Weaponized empathy created at least a decade of violent resistance, seemingly led by native whites.

In terms of story at first glance it shows concerned and liberal outcasts banding together to save the last pregnant girl. A black girl no less. But once you take a closer look your first encounter is an act of random violence, a public bombing by this very organization. It becomes clear that this antifa styled group only wants the girl for their own propaganda and is perfectly willing to kill her to further their goals. The question first presented and left in the air throughout the entire film was why not make her public or even give her to the government. Instead they run and smuggle her through a series of close calls. Ending up in a refugee ghetto. Where they are of course met with violence, before the police state sweeps through. The only thing that stops either side is the truth.

The most telling point at the finale when the world's only known new mother and the white main character find themselves in isolated open water in a tiny row boat. Our empathic white hero bleeds out, his work done. In fact every other character has died at this point. Not so the girl could give birth but to facilitate her delivery to the impossible benevolent non-governmental human project. Something most people regard as a myth and the audience sees zero evidence that they actually exist. The overarching theme of the film is distrust of power and institutions. Be it the authoritarian government, the savage and self interested rebel groups, or the brutal and animalistic refugees anyone in a position of power, however fleeting, quickly turns on the main characters. It is safe to assume that even if the human project were real it would be no less corrupt. But instead we are left with an ambiguous ending. The credits roll just as a fishing boat shows up. Is it an expertly disguised hospital ship? Or more likely just an actual fishing ship, some member of some rebel group likely managed to find a fishing route and invented the story in order to gain access to the pregnant girl. I suspect the latter case is intended. The human project did not exist in the book, it was invented for this film. One final aspect of bleakness in this dwindling future.
